Name: per_item_loo_reliability_and_winners_curse
Title: How Many Retrievals Does a Memory Item Need? Measured Reliability, Winner's Curse and the Pruning Threshold of Per-Item Leave-One-Out Value
Short Hypothesis: For an ALFWorld bank of mixed provenance (expert items plus unfiltered self-written items) read by Qwen3-32B at k=3, the between-item variance of per-item leave-one-out (LOO) value is small relative to game x seed noise even though the bank visibly mixes good and poor items: a per-item rank needs tens of retrievals (split-half reliability below 0.5 at 12 retrievals per half), items selected as top-ranked keep at most half of their apparent excess on fresh re-runs and the loss is predicted out of sample by variance components fitted on disjoint games, LOO-score pruning beats random pruning only above a measured retrieval threshold, and much of what looks like item value is set value: it rises when a same-type neighbour is swapped for a neutral one, pair removal costs more than the sum of single removals, a static procedure prompt absorbs more of it at the item level than the measured +17.2 net set-level residual suggests, and a reader's ranking does not transfer to a second reader. Every quantity is measured by repeated intervention on fresh (game, seed) cells rather than assumed from a noise model.
Related Work: Data Shapley (arXiv:1904.02868) and leave-one-out valuation define item value as marginal utility for deterministic utilities and report no sample-size-to-reliability curve; Data Banzhaf (Wang and Jia 2023; not returned by the literature command, cited from memory) argues rank robustness under a stochastic utility but not for LLM re-runs. Source Attribution in RAG (arXiv:2507.04480) and CUE-R (arXiv:2604.05467) intervene per document in single-shot RAG and report neither seed variance nor re-run cost. Utility pruning and reweighting (ReMe arXiv:2512.10696; SF-AMS arXiv:2607.22562; RoMeRL arXiv:2608.02508) act on scores whose false-prune rates are unmeasured (G10, G24). Compound estimation for binomials (arXiv:2512.25042) and Scorio (arXiv:2603.10960) supply shrinkage and ranking tools for noisy per-unit binomial rates that we reuse offline; VIGOR (arXiv:2607.22002) allocates rollouts by reward variance and motivates the offline adaptive-allocation analysis. Archived counterfactual_memory_screening_under_selection_noise assumed its noise model; memory_item_value_reliability had no intervention arm; both are replaced here by measured variance components with LOO as ground truth, tested out of sample on disjoint games.
Abstract: Every self-evolving memory system scores its items, prunes the bottom and reinforces the top, yet no method reports how many retrievals a per-item value estimate needs before its rank is stable, nor how far the top-scored items regress when re-measured. We treat the noise of the per-item estimator as the estimand, and we measure it on a bank built to contain heterogeneity: expert items, about 200 unfiltered self-written items, 100 planted wrong-procedure items and 20 scene-matched solution items. With Qwen3-32B at k=3 we run leave-one-out re-runs for 1,200 train-stream games x 2 seeds (base plus three single removals), the stream chosen in a free offline retrieval pass so that a 120-item natural panel receives at least 24 retrievals per item in two game-disjoint halves. A crossed mixed model fitted on one game half predicts the split-half reliability and the winner's-curse shrinkage on the other half; both are compared with what is observed, so the noise model is tested rather than assumed. The decision-relevant claim is tested on held-out games screened offline so that every evaluation episode is one whose retrieved set the pruning actually changes: bottom-100 pruning by LOO score estimated from 6 or 24 retrievals per item, against random pruning of the same count (fresh draw per game) and oracle removal of the planted items, 2,200 paired episodes per arm. Composition is manipulated with a neutral token-matched cross-type swap and with named same-type pairs (pair removal versus the sum of single removals), a static3-augmented prompt measures item value net of static credit as a paired net-point drop, a second reader re-measures terciles ranked by the first reader, and a halved store re-measures the pooled single-removal effect. Cost is about 35,000 episodes (about 29 h on two replicas). The output is a retrievals-per-item requirement, an out-of-sample shrinkage factor for selected items, and a pruning threshold below which score-based pruning is indistinguishable from random pruning, each with a confidence interval and a sized falsifier.
Experiments: E0 (free, run first): nested-k position contrast from runs/sweep/k_sweep_final.jsonl (k=1 vs k=3 vs k=7 on the same games) gives per-position value and its game x seed spread; a 500-episode pilot at the pre-registered sampling temperature estimates the seed component and the SD of the paired success difference (0.7 assumed, 0.95 conservative) before any cell is sized. B bank construction: 400 held-out train games at k=0 with one self-written reflection per game, kept regardless of outcome (about 200 usable items of visibly varying quality), 400 episodes; these games are excluded from every later cell. E1 main LOO cell: 1,200 train-stream games x 2 seeds x k=3, base plus 3 single-item removals = 9,600 episodes (about 8 h on two replicas). Bank = expert items + self-written items + 100 planted wrong-procedure items (expert items with one procedural step replaced by a wrong action for the type) + 20 scene-matched solution items (expert trajectory of a same-scene same-type game, so object locations match). Forcing: each planted wrong-procedure item is forced into position 2 or 3 of 10 randomly chosen episodes (1,000 forced episodes, 10 retrievals each); each scene-matched item into the 12 episodes (6 games x 2 seeds) of its scene cluster (240); the remaining 1,160 episodes use the natural retriever set. The 1,200 games are chosen from the 3,553 train games in a free offline retrieval pass, stratified by task type, so that a panel of 120 natural items (>= 80 expert, >= 40 self-written) each receive >= 24 retrievals (>= 12 games x 2 seeds), split into game-disjoint halves A and B with >= 12 retrievals each. Per (item, game, seed): delta = y(S) - y(S minus i), y the success flag. E2 REPLACE ground truth: 150 stream games x 2 seeds x 3 token-matched cross-type replacements = 900 episodes (base from E1); class-level REMOVE vs REPLACE agreement within 5 net (planted, expert, self-written classes) is a pre-registered validity check, panel Spearman reported. E3 composition and additivity: (a) neutral composition, 400 stream games x 2 seeds with positions 1-2 natural and position 3 replaced by a token-matched cross-type expert item (the blind1-type placebo, -3 net under k0 in Measurement C, i.e. near-neutral), base + 3 removals = 3,200 episodes; the same (game, seed) under the natural composition come from E1; the conflict composition (natural top-2 + planted wrong-procedure item) is free from E1's forced episodes. (b) Named pairs: 50 same-type natural pairs co-retrieved in >= 12 stream games (chosen in the free pass) get the pair-removed run on 24 (game, seed) each = 1,200 episodes, plus 15 (natural, planted) pairs x 20 = 300; singles and base come from E1, giving 1,500 quadruples. E4 static-procedure net: 400 stream games x 2 seeds with static3 (3 fixed type-conditioned exemplars, about 430 tokens, cached) prepended to the k=3 prompt, base + 3 removals = 3,200 episodes, paired with E1 on the same (game, seed). E5 pruning decision on held-out games: evaluation bank = expert + self-written + 100 planted (scene-matched items excluded); pruned count = 100 in every arm. Arms: S6 and S24 (bottom 100 by LOO mean from E1 retrievals subsampled to n = 6 and n = 24 per item; items with fewer use all they have), R (random 100, fresh draw per game), O (oracle: the 100 planted). Held-out pool = the 2,353 train games not in the stream or in B, plus the 274 valid games; the retrieved top-3 under every arm is computed offline (free) and U = 1,100 games (stratified by task type) whose retrieved set changes under at least one arm. Each arm runs on U x 2 seeds = 2,200 episodes; 4 arms = 8,800. Contrasts are paired on (game, seed): S6 - R and S24 - R (primary), O - R (positive control), each on the games affected under either arm of the contrast (the rest contribute exactly zero). E6 consumer swap: a second local backbone, served on the second GPU while E5 runs on the first, reads the same retrieved sets (retrieval is reader-independent) on 600 stream games chosen offline so that every panel item receives >= 24 retrievals; base + 3 removals = 4,800 episodes. E7 store size: 50% bank retaining the panel (random half of the remainder), 300 stream games x 2 seeds x 4 = 2,400 episodes. Analyses: crossed mixed model delta ~ item + game + item x composition + residual fitted on game-half A and tested on B; R(n) = var_item / (var_item + var_within / n); split-half correlations by retrieval subsampling within game-disjoint halves (seed replicates of a game stay in one half); winner's-curse slope of half-B2 on half-B1 item means; planted-item detection AUC vs n for LOO, success-conditioned usage count, offline DIG-style confidence gain (extra forward passes, no env steps) and random; empirical-Bayes shrinkage and adaptive re-run allocation as offline analyses of E1 subsamples. Total: 500 + 400 + 9,600 + 900 + 4,700 + 3,200 + 8,800 + 4,800 + 2,400 = 35,300 episodes, about 29 h at the 1,200 episodes/h measured for E1-sized cells on two replicas; E7 is the pre-registered first cut if the pilot throughput is below 1,100/h. Pre-registration of thresholds after E0, B and the pilot.
Baselines and Ablations: Random pruning of the same count (fresh draw per game, so the arm averages over draws) and oracle pruning of the planted items (positive control) bracket score pruning at n = 6 and n = 24; scorers ranked against LOO ground truth on the planted vs panel AUC: success-conditioned usage count (usage-decay family, SF-AMS/ReMe style, unpaired estimator of the same contrast because forcing is randomized), offline DIG-style confidence gain (no env re-runs), random; nested-k position contrast (free) as the cheapest estimator; REMOVE vs REPLACE ground truth (E2); single vs pairwise removal on named pairs (E3b); natural vs neutral vs conflict composition (E1, E3a, E1 forced); gross vs static3-net item value (E4); two readers (E6); two store sizes (E7); raw vs empirical-Bayes-shrunk LOO means and uniform vs adaptive re-run allocation at equal budget, both as offline out-of-sample rank predictions on E1's game halves (no extra episodes). The MemQ-style TD(lambda) scorer and the extra EB-pruning cells of the previous version are dropped to fit the envelope.
Falsifiable Predictions: P1 (headline) Reliability in a mixed-quality bank: on the 120-item natural panel (planted classes excluded), the split-half Spearman of per-item LOO means with n = 12 retrievals per half (game-disjoint halves) is < 0.5 (95% item-bootstrap CI, half-width about 0.13), so R(12) < 0.5 although the bank mixes expert and unfiltered self-written items. Falsified if the split-half Spearman at n = 12 is >= 0.7 with CI excluding 0.5, produced by E1 subsampling when var_item in the mixed bank is large. Out-of-sample model check: variance components fitted on game-half A predict the split-half Spearman within game-half B at n = 3 and n = 6 and the A-vs-B correlation at n = 12; the R(n) model is falsified if two of the three predictions miss the observed value by > 0.15. Positive control: adding the 100 planted wrong-procedure items to the population must raise the n = 12 split-half Spearman by >= 0.2; if it does not, the estimator cannot see heterogeneity that is present and P1 is reported as uninterpretable. P2 Winner's curse, predicted out of sample: the shrinkage s = slope of half-B2 on half-B1 item means (n = 6 per half, game-half B only, 120 items, slope CI about +/-0.14) is <= 0.5, i.e. an item selected on 6 retrievals keeps at most half its apparent excess on fresh re-runs, and s matches the Gaussian empirical-Bayes prediction computed from game-half A's variance components within 0.15. Falsified if s >= 0.75 with CI excluding 0.5, or if the out-of-sample prediction misses s by > 0.15 (which the model allows only if item effects are game-specific or heavy-tailed). Top-decile retention (select on B1, measure on B2) is reported with its wide CI; the decision is by the slope. Positive control: with the 20 scene-matched solution items in the selection pool (n = 6 per half), the top decile must retain >= 0.8 of its apparent excess; if real excess is not retained, P2 is uninterpretable. P3 Pruning threshold (E5, paired on (game, seed) over affected games, about 1,750 informative pairs per contrast, CI +/-3.3 net at the pilot SD 0.7, +/-4.5 at 0.95; margin M = max(5 net, CI half-width + 2 net), fixed at pre-registration): P3a, S6 - R is within M of zero (score pruning from 6 retrievals per item is indistinguishable from random pruning); falsified if S6 beats R by more than M with CI excluding 0. P3b, S24 - R >= M; falsified if S24 - R < M - 3 with CI excluding M. Positive control: O - R >= M + 3 net; if it is not, the P3 nulls are reported as uninterpretable rather than as findings. P4 Detection: LOO reaches AUC >= 0.8 for the 100 planted wrong-procedure items against the 120 panel items at n = 10 retrievals per item, and the success-conditioned usage count on the same episodes reaches at most LOO AUC - 0.12; falsified if usage-count AUC at n = 10 is >= LOO AUC - 0.05 with the paired item-bootstrap CI on delta-AUC excluding 0.12 (pre-registered CI half-width <= 0.06 from 100 vs 120 items). Produced by E1's forced episodes, where randomized forcing makes the usage count an unpaired estimator of the same contrast; it wins if game variance is small relative to seed variance. AUC-vs-n curves at n in {3, 6, 10} are reported for all scorers. P5 Set value: (a) neutral composition, the pooled single-removal effect of position 1-2 panel items is higher by >= 5 net under the neutral cross-type third item than under the natural composition on the same (game, seed) (1,600 paired removals, CI +/-3.9 net); falsified if the paired rise is <= 1 net with CI excluding 5, the outcome if the reader's use of an item does not depend on its neighbours; the item x composition variance component is reported as secondary. (b) Additivity, over 50 named same-type natural pairs (1,200 quadruples, CI +/-5 net at SD 0.9) pair removal costs more than the sum of the two single removals by >= 8 net (LOO under-credits redundant items); falsified if the pooled excess is < 2 net with CI excluding 8. The 15 (natural, planted) pairs are reported as exploratory. P6 Consumer swap and store size: (a) transfer, terciles of the natural panel are formed by reader A's LOO mean on game-half A (n about 12); positive control, reader A's own top-minus-bottom gap on game-half B must be >= 8 net (else the ranking carries nothing to transfer and P6a is reported as uninterpretable); prediction, reader B's top-minus-bottom gap on the same terciles (E6, >= 24 retrievals per item, 960 effects per tercile, gap CI +/-4 net) is <= 3 net; falsified if >= 8 net with CI excluding 3, the outcome if item value is reader-independent. Raw and disattenuated panel Spearman across readers are reported with bootstrap CIs as secondary. Second positive control: the planted wrong-procedure class harms reader B by >= 5 net (class CI +/-4) or reader B is item-insensitive and P6a is uninterpretable. (b) Store size, halving the bank raises the pooled single-removal effect of retrieved items on the same games by >= 4 net (E7 vs E1, game-paired, 1,800 removals, difference CI +/-2.6 net) because retrieved sets lose same-type redundancy; falsified if the rise is <= 1 net with CI excluding 4. P7 Static net, stated against Measurement C: the set-level residual of k=3 over static3 is +17.2 net [+11.9, +22.4] (58% of the +29.6 gain over k0). Prediction: at the item level static3 absorbs a larger share, the pooled single-removal effect of natural panel items under static3 + k3 is at least 5 net below its value under k3 alone on the same (game, seed) (E4 vs E1, 2,400 paired removals, CI +/-2.4 net); falsified if the paired drop is below 2 net with CI excluding 5, the outcome if static exemplars and retrieved items are additive, which the +17.2 residual does not rule out. The set-level (static3 + k3) - k3 contrast on the same 400 games is reported alongside (CI +/-4.5). Pre-registered rule: if the pilot's gross single-removal effect is below 4 net, P7 is declared underpowered and E4 is reported as a measurement.
Measurement and Noise Control: All contrasts are paired on (game, seed); CIs by two-way cluster bootstrap over games and items (items cross games); variance components from a crossed mixed model with the seed component measured in the pilot and reported first; model-derived R(n) is fitted on game-half A and tested against observed correlations on game-half B, never on the same games. Per-item retrievals are counted as (game, seed) cells; split halves are game-disjoint so seed replicates of one game never straddle halves. Panel coverage (120 items x >= 24 retrievals in E1, >= 24 in E6) is guaranteed before any episode by the free offline retrieval pass; if the pass cannot reach 120 natural items, the panel is set to the largest number that reaches 24 (>= 100) and the CI half-widths are recomputed at pre-registration. Power: with within-item SD of delta about 0.45 (pilot), a class CI of +/-5 net needs about 320 effects; the planted class has 100 x 10 = 1,000; tercile classes have 40 x 24 = 960 (+/-2.8 net, gap +/-4); paired removal contrasts (E3a, E4, E7) use 1,600-2,400 paired effects at SD 0.6-0.8 (+/-2.4 to +/-3.9 net); quadruples use 1,200 at SD 0.9 (+/-5 net); E5 contrasts use about 1,750 informative pairs (+/-3.3 net at SD 0.7, +/-4.5 at 0.95, both measured in the pilot); the winner's-curse slope over 120 items has CI about +/-0.14; the paired delta-AUC from 100 planted vs 120 panel items has half-width about 0.06 (bootstrap, checked before pre-registration). Margin rule (pre-registered): every net-point margin is at least the cell's CI half-width plus 2 net, minimum 5 net; margins are never lowered to fit a small effect, and a claim whose cell cannot reach its margin is declared underpowered rather than tested. Reliability curves use retrieval subsampling without replacement; disattenuation, where reported, uses each arm's own split-half reliability and is secondary to equal-n or class-level comparisons. Thresholds, cells and stopping rules are pre-registered after E0, B and the pilot; both replicas stay busy (E1 spans both; E5 on one while the second backbone serves E6 on the other; E7 and E2-E4 fill gaps) and episodes/min and vLLM queue depth are logged per cell.
Preprint Collision Check: All queries answered by the literature command (Semantic Scholar + HF Papers, both channels ok); WebSearch not used. (1) home: 'winner's curse regression to the mean selecting top-ranked noisy estimates shrinkage empirical Bayes' (no recency filter): no pre-emption; nearest are Compound Estimation for Binomials arXiv:2512.25042 (EB shrinkage of binomial rates across units; a tool we adopt) and Scorio arXiv:2603.10960 (statistical ranking of LLMs under repeated sampling); nothing on selection bias of per-item value estimates. (2) mechanism, --recent: 'per-item value of retrieved memory leave-one-out noise seeds sample size LLM agent': no per-item noise study; Memory Reward Inflation / Echo Gap arXiv:2608.00017 (self-graded rewards inflate wrong episodes; not counterfactual, not per-item), MEMPROBE arXiv:2606.24595 (audits memory content, not item value). (3) closest named method: 'leave-one-out data valuation rank stability variance number of samples Data Shapley convergence': Data Shapley arXiv:1904.02868, OddSHAP arXiv:2602.01399, shapiq arXiv:2410.01649, FreeShap arXiv:2406.04606; none reports rank stability under a stochastic LLM utility or in agents. (4) 'Data Banzhaf robust data valuation noisy utility stochastic training rank consistency': empty on both channels; retry 'Data Banzhaf robust data valuation' returned Distributionally Robust Data Valuation (ICML 2024), DeRDaVa arXiv:2312.11413, Eigen-Value arXiv:2510.23409, For-Value arXiv:2508.10180; the Data Banzhaf paper itself was not returned and is cited from memory. (5) --recent 'progress-based surrogate outcome instead of binary success variance reduction LLM agent evaluation fewer rollouts' surfaced VIGOR arXiv:2607.22002 (variance-based rollout allocation), used only as motivation for the offline adaptive-allocation analysis. No preprint measures retrievals-to-reliability, out-of-sample winner's-curse shrinkage or a pruning threshold for memory items.
Risk Factors and Limitations: If the reader is near-deterministic at the served temperature, the seed component is near zero and noise is carried by games; the pilot reports this and the design still holds because retrievals span games. The mixed-provenance bank may fail to create heterogeneity (self-written items uniformly mediocre): the pre-registered check is that the self-written and expert classes differ by >= 3 net or the panel split-half r at n = 12 is >= 0.3; if both fail, P1 rests on the planted positive control and is reported as such. Choosing stream games for panel coverage biases the game distribution; selection is stratified by task type and the coverage table is reported; class-level results are also given on the unselected remainder of the stream. Planted wrong-procedure items may be detected at n = 3, making the threshold uninformative for that class; the natural-panel reliability curve is the primary result. Heavy-tailed item effects would break the Gaussian EB prediction in P2, which is itself a reportable outcome. If planted items are rarely retrieved in the held-out pool, the O arm's affected set is small; the free offline pass reports it and O is then evaluated on its affected games only with its own CI. If the second backbone cannot be served alongside the first, E6 is scheduled after E5 on both GPUs (same episode count, +2 h). Retrieval frequency is confounded with item genericity; analyses are stratified by task type. Compute is about 29 h on two A100s at 1,200 episodes/h; E7 is the first cut if throughput is lower.
Addresses gap: G24 (variance, cross-seed stability and sample cost of per-item estimates are unreported, now with the noise model tested out of sample); secondarily G22 (proxy scorers are ranked against LOO ground truth with a sized delta-AUC) and G25 (composition is a manipulated arm with a neutral swap and named pairs).
Not a restatement of: Nearest brief bullet: 'Noise floor ... per-item estimates will be far noisier than per-arm ones; any item-level claim must be about a distribution of items or a manufactured class' - the brief anticipates the noise; this idea measures its variance components on a bank built to contain heterogeneity, turns them into a retrievals-per-item requirement, an out-of-sample winner's-curse shrinkage and a pruning threshold, and tests each against fresh re-runs on screened held-out games. Nearest digest card: arXiv:2507.04480 (Shapley attribution in RAG; stability across repeated LLM calls not evaluated) - this idea makes stability, cost and decision utility the estimands, in a multi-step agent with seeds, compositions, pairs and readers as arms. Nearest archived idea: counterfactual_memory_screening_under_selection_noise assumed the noise model; here it is fitted on one game half and tested on the other; memory_item_value_reliability lacked an intervention arm; here LOO/REPLACE re-runs are the ground truth and every claim is class- or distribution-level with stated power and a margin rule that cannot shrink below the CI.
Changes made: P1: population changed from a uniform expert bank to a mixed-provenance bank (new 400-episode self-written pass B, unfiltered) with a 120-item panel at >= 24 retrievals guaranteed by free offline stream selection; the algebraic '0.8 only at n >= 40' clause replaced by an out-of-sample test of the R(n) model (fit on game-half A, test at three n on half B); the planted class added as a positive control for the reliability curve. P2: shrinkage is now the half-B2-on-half-B1 slope (CI +/-0.14) compared with an EB prediction from game-disjoint half A, so agreement is no longer by construction; 20 scene-matched solution items added as a positive tail and positive control; the top-decile ratio demoted to a reported statistic. P3: E5 moved to a held-out pool screened offline so every evaluation episode is affected under some arm; 2,200 paired episodes per arm (CI +/-3.3 net at the pilot SD, sized in the Measurement section); grid cut to n in {6, 24}, one random arm with a fresh draw per game, the oracle; the margin rule is now max(5, CI + 2) instead of half the oracle effect. P4: planted class raised from 40 to 100 items (10 forced retrievals each); delta-AUC margin 0.12 with a paired item-bootstrap CI (half-width <= 0.06) pre-registered; the unmeasurable '3x retrievals' clause dropped. P5: the composition contrast is a neutral token-matched cross-type swap (the conflict composition is free from E1's forced episodes and is a control); the estimand is a paired net-point rise (+/-3.9) instead of a ratio to var_item; the pair clause is redefined over 50 named same-type pairs x 24 quadruples with a pooled super-additivity claim (+/-5 net). P6: the item-rank disattenuation claim is replaced by a class-level transfer test (terciles chosen by reader A on game-half A, re-measured by reader B, 960 effects per tercile, gap CI +/-4) with reader A's own out-of-sample gap and the planted class as positive controls; E6 enlarged to 4,800 episodes with guaranteed panel coverage; the store-size claim restated as a game-paired redundancy rise (+/-2.6 net). P7: the surviving-fraction ratio replaced by a paired net-point drop of the pooled single-removal effect under static3 + k3 vs k3 (E4 3,200 episodes, +/-2.4 net), stated against Measurement C's +17.2 set-level residual with the set-level contrast reported alongside. Budget: E2 halved (900), the three random-draw cells, the EB-shrunk pruning cells and the MemQ scorer cut, the separate conflict-composition arm dropped (free from E1); EB shrinkage and adaptive allocation are offline analyses; total 35,300 episodes, about 29 h, versus 34,000 / 28 h before, with E7 as the pre-registered first cut. Novelty kept: the core claim (per-item LOO value is mostly game x seed noise plus set value, ranks need tens of retrievals, selected items regress, pruning has a retrieval threshold) is unchanged and is now made on a heterogeneous bank, where it is harder to satisfy, and the composition, pair, store-size and static claims all name one mechanism, same-type redundancy making LOO under-credit items, so they can jointly fail.
